summary:
This is the opening page of **chapter 8, Image classification**. The box *This chapter covers* lists four topics:

- Understanding convolutional neural networks (**ConvNets**)
- Using **data augmentation** to mitigate overfitting
- Using a **pretrained ConvNet for feature extraction**
- **Fine-tuning** a pretrained ConvNet

The introduction sets the historical scene. Computer vision was *the first big success story of deep learning* and drove its initial rise between 2011 and 2015. Convolutional neural networks began getting remarkably good results on image classification competitions: first **Dan Ciresan** won two niche competitions (the **ICDAR 2011** Chinese character recognition competition and the **IJCNN 2011** German traffic signs recognition competition), and then, more notably, in fall **2012** **Hinton's group** won the high-profile **ImageNet** large-scale visual recognition challenge. Many more promising results followed in other vision tasks.

The second paragraph begins a twist: these early successes *weren't quite enough to make deep learning mainstream at the time; it took a few years*. The sentence continues on p.256, which describes the skepticism of the computer vision community until 2016.

How to use this page: treat the bullet list as the chapter roadmap. Section 8.1 (p.256) introduces ConvNets with an MNIST example and explains convolution (p.258) and max pooling (p.263); 8.2 (p.265) trains a ConvNet from scratch on a small dataset and introduces data augmentation (p.276); 8.3 (p.280) covers feature extraction and fine-tuning with a pretrained model.

paragraphs.excerpt: Computer vision was the first big success story of deep learning.
paragraphs.what_it_says: ConvNets produced the first big deep learning successes: Ciresan's wins at ICDAR 2011 and IJCNN 2011, then Hinton's group winning ImageNet in fall 2012.
paragraphs.what_it_means: Image classification benchmarks were where deep learning first clearly beat established methods, which is why vision is the natural first application chapter.
paragraphs.why_it_matters: Gives historical motivation for studying ConvNets before other architectures.

terminology.meaning: A neural network built from convolution layers that learn local, translation-invariant patterns; introduced in detail from p.256.
Large-scale visual recognition competition on the ImageNet dataset; the 2012 win is the one referred to here.

paragraphs.what_it_means: Scientific adoption lags behind results; established research communities need time to change methods.

concepts.name: Convolutional neural network (ConvNet)
concepts.definition: A deep learning model built from convolution and pooling layers, used by most computer vision applications.
concepts.intuition: Learns small visual patterns that can appear anywhere in an image and combines them into larger ones.
concepts.technical: Introduced on p.256 with Conv2D and MaxPooling2D layers; convolution explained from p.258.
concepts.significance: Drove deep learning's first big successes (2011-2015).
concepts.example: The 2012 ImageNet-winning network from Hinton's group.
concepts.misconception: That ConvNets became mainstream immediately after 2012; the authors say it took until about 2016.

takeaways: Chapter 8 covers ConvNets, data augmentation, feature extraction with pretrained ConvNets, and fine-tuning.
